messages:
mira: Heads-up — NVIDIA just pushed driver 535.86.10 with CVE-2026-12345 noted as possible local privilege escalation when X driver exposed. Need a quick triage for Dedicated + Private fleets. @john @sam can you look?

john: on it. can you paste the advisory link?

mira: https://nvidia.example.com/security/advisory/535.86.10 (copied key excerpt). they call out module ioctl paths.

sam: quick checklist: which node images use the affected driver? Dedicated pool image tags v1.8.2 and on-prem images (ami-gpu-2025-03) are suspect.

lee: I can run a fast inventory. running this on a node shows: `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv` -> 535.86.8 on prod-dedicated-1, 535.86.10 on canary-2.

kevin: TL;DR: we already have 535.86.10 in canary? that's odd — who rolled that? ops-bot: deploy-bot reports driver-rollforward/2026-03-10 applied to canary-2 at 2026-03-10T02:14Z.

mira: good to know. Sam, prioritize exploitability: is this network-exposed or requires login?

sam: vendor says local auth required (local user). but on Dedicated we have shared developer access and some CI runners with GPU access. that increases blast radius. risk: medium-high for Dedicated; lower for Private if nodes are locked down.

john: mitigation options: 1) immediate kernel module hardening + RBAC to restrict who can load/unload modules, 2) audit log changes for module events, 3) patch driver to patched build if vendor provides hotpatch.

lee: for RBAC: propose adding a PSP/PodSecurity admission exception? actually we should adjust node-level sudoers and remove developer sudo on GPU nodes. That needs coordination with infra.

mira: can we attach an emergency rule to deny privileged Pods on Dedicated GPU node pool until we finish triage? simple k8s label + taint + admission policy should do.

kevin: I can prepare a canary policy: `kubectl label nodes gpu-canary dedicated-rollforward=true` and then run an OPA gate to block privileged pods on nodes without 'gpu-safe' label.

sam: testing matrix for compatibility validation we need: CUDA runtime smoke, cuDNN conv tests, NCCL collective sync, and model-serving inference with seq lengths we normally see. Keep it under 5 minute per node. Example script snippet:

```
# smoke test
python -c "import torch;print(torch.cuda.is_available())"
# run a mini allreduce with nccl
/usr/local/cuda/samples/1_Utilities/deviceQuery/deviceQuery
```

john: also verify KMS integration: confirm driver upgrade doesn't break encrypted model mounts (we use KMS + dm-crypt on on-prem). Check kernel crypto modules remain loaded and keyctl access isn't affected.

lee: noted. I'll add a quick KMS check: `ls /dev/mapper` and `cryptsetup status <mapper>` in smoke.

ops-bot: action created: SEC-TRIAGE-2026-043 assigned to @sam, @lee, due 2026-03-11T12:00Z.

mira: patch prioritization: Dedicated = P1 (because shared access), Private on-prem = P2 unless customer reports, Hosted API instances = P3 (we don't expose driver to customers directly). We need rollback plan if patched driver breaks performance.

kevin: rollback steps: keep previous driver package in object storage, have kube-driver-operator config to pin driver version, and a canary rollback job. I'll draft a runbook.

sam: one more: enable extra audit logging for module events and container exec on GPU nodes. send logs to Splunk with tag `gpu-driver-triage`. That will help detect any attempted exploitation.

mira: agreed. Also confirm any PCIe firmware updates are separate; don't mix firmware with driver patch in same window.

john: OK I'll draft a short PR for the emergency k8s admission policy and the runbook. @sec-bot please record the triage summary in the incident tracker.

sec-bot: incident record created: IR-2026-239 (gpu-driver-cve), severity: elevated, linked tickets: SEC-TRIAGE-2026-043.

kevin: ETA for canary full compatibility results ~4 hours. If green, propose a staged rollout 10% -> 30% -> 100% over 12 hours with perf gates.

mira: thanks all. keep updates here. paste quick failures as code blocks. :eyes:
